scenario: I am an employee of a bank in Germany. I have many loyal customers who trust me and my bank. Among them is one family of five who is deeply in debt and does not fulfill the conditions for being granted another loan. I see an undetectable way to temporarily redirect money from another account into the family's account, allowing them to qualify for the loan. At the same time, I would abuse the trust of the other customers and of my colleagues. But if I do this, I will be able to prevent the family from taking their eldest child out of college.
choice: I decide to temporarily redirect money from another account into the family's account
entities: I,1 eldest child in the indebted family of five,1 other member of the indebted family of five,1 other member of the indebted family of five,1 other member of the indebted family of five,1 other member of the indebted family of five,1 customer whose account would be temporarily redirected from,1+ other loyal customers whose trust would be abused, excluding the indebted family and the redirected-from account holder,1+ bank colleagues whose trust would be abused
outcomes: The family's account appears to meet the loan conditions.
The family is able to continue the loan application.
The family experiences short-term financial relief.
The eldest child stays in college for the time being.
The other account holder has less money available in their account.
The other account holder is exposed to financial disruption.
I abuse the trust of other customers.
I put the bank's funds and processes at risk.
